title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
authors: Yao, S.; Shinn, N.; Razavi, P.; Narasimhan, K.
abstract: Benchmark emulating dynamic conversations between an LLM-simulated user and a language agent with domain-specific API tools (retail and airline). Introduces the pass^k reliability metric over multiple trials. Shows that even gpt-4o succeeds on <50% of tasks and pass^8 < 25% in retail. Foundational reference for tool-using agent benchmarks; also highlights reliability problems.

title: τ²-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment
authors: Barres, V.; Dong, H.; Ray, S.; Si, X.; Narasimhan, K.
abstract: Extends τ-bench to a dual-control environment where simulated users can also take actions and call tools, capturing real-world scenarios like technical customer support. Adds a telecom domain and more demanding interaction patterns. Successor benchmark to τ-bench.

title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
authors: Liu, X.; Yu, H.; Zhang, H.; Xu, Y.; Lei, X.; Lai, H.; Gu, Y.; Ding, H.; Men, K.; Yang, K.; Zhang, S.; Deng, X.; Zeng, A.; Du, Z.; Zhang, C.; Shen, S.; Zhang, T.; Su, Y.; Sun, H.; Huang, M.; Dong, Y.; Tang, J.
abstract: First multi-environment benchmark to evaluate LLMs as autonomous agents across 8 distinct environments (5 newly designed). Establishes a general framework for agent evaluation beyond single task-completion metrics. Widely cited as a baseline for tool-using agent capability.

title: The Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL): From Tool Use to Agentic Evaluation of Large Language Models
authors: Yan, F.; Mao, H.; Ji, C. C.-J.; Zhang, T.; Patil, S. G.; Stoica, I.; Gonzalez, J. E.
abstract: Comprehensive benchmark for function calling (tool use) in LLMs, evaluating serial and parallel calls across programming languages using AST-based evaluation. Tests abstention and multi-step agentic reasoning. De facto standard for function-calling evaluation.

title: AgentHallu: Benchmarking Automated Hallucination Attribution of LLM-based Agents
authors: Liu, X.; Yang, X.; Li, Z.; Li, P.; He, R.
abstract: 693 high-quality agent trajectories across 7 frameworks and 5 domains, with a taxonomy of 5 hallucination categories (Planning, Retrieval, Reasoning, Human-Interaction, Tool-Use) and 14 sub-categories. Human-curated multi-level annotations for step-level localization. Evaluates 13 leading models; best achieves only 41.1% step localization, tool-use hallucinations hardest at 11.6%. MUST CITE — overlapping title and closely adjacent contribution.

title: LLM-based Agents Suffer from Hallucinations: A Survey of Taxonomy, Methods, and Directions
authors: Lin, X. and 19 others
abstract: First comprehensive survey of hallucinations specifically in LLM-based agents. Analyzes the full workflow of agents, proposes a taxonomy across stages, examines 18 triggering causes, and reviews mitigation methods. Directly relevant to the propagation framing of AgentHallu-Bench.

title: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Language Models: Principles, Taxonomy, Challenges, and Open Questions
authors: Huang, L.; Yu, W.; Ma, W.; Zhong, W.; Feng, Z.; Wang, H.; Chen, Q.; Peng, W.; Feng, X.; Qin, B.; Liu, T.
abstract: Published in ACM TOIS — a venue IP&M readers respect. Provides an innovative taxonomy of hallucination in LLMs, factors contributing to hallucination, detection methods, and benchmarks. Central reference for hallucination classification; the paper is explicitly framed around implications for IR systems.

title: A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of Large Language Model-based Agents
authors: Zhang, Z.; Bo, X.; Ma, C.; Li, R.; Chen, X.; Dai, Q.; Zhu, J.; Dong, Z.; Wen, J.-R.
abstract: ACM TOIS survey of memory mechanisms in LLM-based agents. Relevant for framing agent pipelines, memory-accumulation error modes (scoped out as P3 in AgentHallu-Bench), and positioning agent research within IS venues.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
authors: Zheng, L.; Chiang, W.-L.; Sheng, Y.; Zhuang, S.; Wu, Z.; Zhuang, Y.; Lin, Z.; Li, Z.; Li, D.; Xing, E.; Zhang, H.; Gonzalez, J. E.; Stoica, I.
abstract: Foundational LLM-as-judge paper. Establishes that GPT-4 agrees with human expert judgment above κ=0.8 in pairwise preference. Essential baseline for any κ-based judge validation work including AgentHallu-Bench's κ=0.432 result.

title: A Survey on LLM-as-a-Judge
authors: Gu, J.; Jiang, X.; Shi, Z.; Tan, H.; Zhai, X.; Xu, C.; Li, W.; Shen, Y.; Ma, S.; Liu, H.; Wang, S.; Zhang, K.; Wang, Y.; Gao, W.; Ni, L.; Guo, J.
abstract: Comprehensive survey of LLM-as-a-Judge methods. Addresses strategies to enhance reliability including consistency, bias mitigation, and adapting judges to diverse scenarios. Direct context for AgentHallu-Bench's ensemble judge design.

title: Can You Trust LLM Judgments? Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge
authors: Schroeder, K.; Wood-Doughty, Z.
abstract: Introduces a framework for rigorously evaluating reliability of LLM judgments using McDonald's omega. Directly relevant to AgentHallu-Bench's judge validation methodology; argues for quantitative reliability measurement rather than assumed validity.

title: Judging the Judges: Evaluating Alignment and Vulnerabilities in LLMs-as-Judges
authors: Thakur, A. S.; Choudhary, K.; Srinik, V.; Hupkes, D.
abstract: Quantifies alignment and vulnerabilities across judge models. Uses Scott's π and percent agreement, finds Llama3 70B and GPT-4 Turbo reach excellent alignment but still below human baseline. Reports systematic biases and inconsistencies across judges.

title: LLMs instead of Human Judges? A Large Scale Empirical Study across 20 NLP Evaluation Tasks
authors: Bavaresco, A.; Testoni, A.; Poesio, M.; Paun, S.; Uma, A.; Fornaciari, T.; Hovy, D.; Plank, B.; Bernardi, R.
abstract: Large-scale empirical study of LLMs as judges across 20 NLP tasks. Reports correlation and agreement metrics with human judges. Shows variable agreement across tasks, supporting the caution in AgentHallu-Bench about treating ensemble judges as absolute ground truth.

title: Judge's Verdict: A Comprehensive Analysis of LLM Judge Capability through Human Agreement
authors: (authors, 2025)
abstract: Benchmark for judge capability measured by Cohen's κ agreement with humans rather than correlation, on RAG and agentic pipeline outputs. Directly adjacent to AgentHallu-Bench's κ validation approach.

title: How Reliable is Multilingual LLM-as-a-Judge?
authors: Fu, X.; and colleagues
abstract: Shows LLM judges exhibit inconsistency across languages (via Fleiss/Cohen κ). Majority-vote ensembles reduce per-language variability but no approach reaches full cross-lingual reliability. Relevant for limitations of ensemble judging in AgentHallu-Bench.

title: Don't Use LLMs to Make Relevance Judgments
authors: Soboroff, I.
abstract: Argues against using LLMs as automated relevance assessors in IR evaluation. Provides a skeptical counterpoint from the IR community that should be acknowledged in AgentHallu-Bench's judge-reliability discussion. Directly relevant to the evaluation-focused framing.

title: Large Language Models can Accurately Predict Searcher Preferences
authors: Thomas, P.; Spielman, S.; Craswell, N.; Mitra, B.
abstract: SIGIR 2024 paper showing LLMs can predict searcher preferences with high agreement. Counterpoint to Soboroff 2024. Essential IR-venue reference for framing AgentHallu-Bench within the SIGIR community's evaluation debate.

title: LLMs can be fooled into labelling a document as relevant
authors: Alaofi, M.; Thomas, P.; Scholer, F.; Sanderson, M.
abstract: Demonstrates adversarial manipulation of LLM-based relevance judgments in IR. Supports AgentHallu-Bench's caution about treating automated judges as infallible. IR-community framing.

title: Rankers, Judges, and Assistants: Towards Understanding the Interplay of LLMs in Information Retrieval Evaluation
authors: Balog, K.; Metzler, D.; Qin, Z.
abstract: Analyzes the interplay between LLMs used as rankers, judges, and assistants in IR evaluation. Directly relevant to IP&M audience and the evaluation-focused framing of AgentHallu-Bench.

title: MCPAgentBench: A Real-world Task Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agent MCP Tool Use
authors: (authors, 2026)
abstract: Benchmark for Model Context Protocol tool use with authentic tasks and simulated MCP tools in a dynamic sandbox. Evaluates tool selection with distractors. Contemporary comparison point for AgentHallu-Bench's tool-use focus.

title: MCPVerse: An Expansive, Real-World Benchmark for Agentic Tool Use
authors: (authors, 2025)
abstract: Addresses limitations of benchmarks that use artificial tools by providing an expansive real-world tool-use benchmark. Tests agent robustness under realistic API execution. Peer benchmark to AgentHallu-Bench.

title: T-Eval: Evaluating the Tool Utilization Capability of Large Language Models Step by Step
authors: Chen, Z.; Du, W.; Zhang, W.; Liu, K.; Liu, J.; Zheng, M.; Zhuo, J.; Zhang, S.; Lin, D.; Chen, K.; Zhao, F.
abstract: Step-by-step evaluation of tool utilization in LLMs. Decomposes tool use into sub-capabilities (instruction following, planning, reasoning, retrieval, understanding, review). Precedent for stage-decomposed evaluation like AgentHallu-Bench's 4-stage cascade.

title: Evaluation and Benchmarking of LLM Agents: A Survey
authors: Yehudai, A. and co-authors
abstract: KDD 2025 survey consolidating agent evaluation across behaviour, capability, reliability, and safety. Taxonomy of evaluation objectives. Core reference for positioning AgentHallu-Bench within the agent evaluation landscape.

title: Survey on Evaluation of LLM-based Agents
authors: Yehudai, A.; Eden, L.; Li, A.; Uziel, G.; Zhao, Y.; Bar-Haim, R.; Cohan, A.; Shmueli-Scheuer, M.
abstract: Companion survey reviewing 60+ agent benchmarks and frameworks. Discusses benchmark design, reliability probing, and robustness stress-tests. Useful for the related work section.

title: A Survey of Large Language Model Empowered Agents for Recommendation and Search: Towards Next-Generation Information Retrieval
authors: Xie, X.; Li, X.; Wang, H.; Yang, Z.; Lv, Q.; Yu, L.
abstract: First systematic review classifying LLM agents in recommendation and IR. Frames agent research explicitly for the IR community. Essential for tying AgentHallu-Bench to the IP&M audience.

title: Large Language Models for Information Retrieval: A Survey
authors: Zhu, Y.; Dou, Z.; Liu, Z.; and co-authors
abstract: Comprehensive survey of LLMs for IR. Core reference to connect to the IR community. Multiple updates through 2025 reflect field's pace.

title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Es, S.; James, J.; Espinosa-Anke, L.; Schockaert, S.
abstract: Automated RAG evaluation framework using LLM-based metrics for context relevance, faithfulness, and answer relevance. Precedent for multi-judge evaluation in RAG, relevant to AgentHallu-Bench's ensemble design.

title: RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Niu, C.; Wu, Y.; Zhu, J.; Xu, S.; Shum, K.; Zhong, R.; Song, J.; Zhang, T.
abstract: Large-scale span-level human-annotated hallucination corpus for RAG. Reference for human-annotated ground truth in hallucination evaluation; directly relevant to AgentHallu-Bench's 100-label human validation.

title: SelfCheckGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection for Generative Large Language Models
authors: Manakul, P.; Liusie, A.; Gales, M. J. F.
abstract: Black-box hallucination detection via sampling-based self-consistency. Foundational for self-consistency baselines; AgentHallu-Bench's k=3 self-consistency mitigation is in this lineage.

title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
authors: Wang, X.; Wei, J.; Schuurmans, D.; Le, Q. V.; Chi, E. H.; Narang, S.; Chowdhery, A.; Zhou, D.
abstract: Original self-consistency paper. Direct citation for AgentHallu-Bench's self-consistency mitigation comparison.

title: Semantic Entropy for Detecting Confabulations in Large Language Models
authors: Farquhar, S.; Kossen, J.; Kuhn, L.; Gal, Y.
abstract: Nature paper on meaning-level uncertainty for detecting confabulations without task-specific training. High-profile reference for principled hallucination detection; complementary to AgentHallu-Bench's stage-decomposed metric.

title: LLM-Check: Investigating Detection of Hallucinations in Large Language Models
authors: Sriramanan, G.; Bharti, S.; Sadasivan, V. S.; Saha, S.; Kattakinda, P.; Feizi, S.
abstract: Uses internal attention maps, hidden activations and output probabilities to detect hallucinations in single LLM responses. Useful counterpoint — AgentHallu-Bench operates at a coarser (stage) granularity and on agent pipelines rather than standalone outputs.

title: The Illusion of Progress: Re-evaluating Hallucination Detection in LLMs
authors: (authors, 2025)
abstract: Shows hallucination detection methods drop dramatically when evaluated against human-aligned metrics instead of ROUGE. Directly reinforces AgentHallu-Bench's evaluation-critique that heuristic metrics overestimate method effectiveness.

title: AgentSpec: Customizable Runtime Enforcement for Safe and Reliable LLM Agents
authors: Wang, H.; and co-authors
abstract: Runtime enforcement framework for LLM agents with rule-based predicates and enforcement actions (user inspection, LLM self-examination, action invocation). Direct comparison point for AgentHallu-Bench's three-layer interceptor.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
authors: Debenedetti, E.; Zhang, J.; Balunović, M.; Beurer-Kellner, L.; Fischer, M.; Tramèr, F.
abstract: Dynamic benchmark for prompt injection attacks and defenses in LLM agents. Relevant for positioning AgentHallu-Bench's injection-based methodology — AgentDojo targets adversarial injections; AgentHallu-Bench targets benign semantic injections for evaluation.

title: SABER: Small Actions, Big Errors — Safeguarding Mutating Steps in LLM Agents
authors: Cuadron, A.; Yu, P.; Liu, Y.; Gupta, A.
venue: ICLR Workshop on Memory for LLM-Based Agentic Systems
abstract: Safeguarding approach for mutating steps in LLM agents. Informed recent task-quality fixes in τ²-bench. Relevant for AgentHallu-Bench's interceptor story.

title: Automated Hallucination Correction for AI Agents: A Case Study on τ²-Bench
authors: Cleanlab authors
abstract: Industry report showing LLM trust scoring with fallback strategies automatically cuts τ²-bench agent failure rates by up to 50%. Supporting reference for runtime trustworthiness scoring; complementary to AgentHallu-Bench's rule-based interceptor.

title: Mitigating LLM Hallucinations Using a Multi-Agent Framework
authors: Darwish, A. M.; Rashed, E. A.; Khoriba, G.
abstract: Multi-agent framework with rule-based logic to constrain LLM behavior and mitigate hallucinations. Comparison point for AgentHallu-Bench's multi-layer interceptor design.

title: Toward Mitigation of Hallucination for LLM-empowered Agents: Progressive Generalization Bound Exploration and Watchdog Monitor (HalMit)
authors: Liu, S.; Liu, W.; Xu, Z.; Wang, X.; and co-authors
abstract: Watchdog monitor approach for mitigating hallucinations in LLM-empowered agents via probabilistic fractal sampling and generalization bound. Comparable to AgentHallu-Bench's runtime interceptor but more complex.

title: Mitigating Reasoning Hallucination through Multi-Agent Collaborative Filtering
authors: (authors)
abstract: Expert Systems with Applications — an IS-adjacent journal. Multi-agent collaborative filtering to mitigate reasoning hallucinations. Useful IS-venue citation.

title: A Benchmark for Evaluating Crisis Information Generation Capabilities in LLMs (CIEval)
authors: Han, R.; An, L.; Zhou, W.; Li, G.
abstract: Information Research journal benchmark for LLM crisis information generation. Demonstrates IS-community interest in domain-specific LLM benchmarks; relevant venue precedent for AgentHallu-Bench.

title: Towards Robust QA Evaluation via Open LLMs
authors: Kamalloo, E.; Upadhyay, S.; Lin, J.
abstract: SIGIR 2024 short paper on robust QA evaluation via open LLMs. Supports the case that LLM-based evaluators are viable when validated. Core IR-venue reference.

title: Evaluating Retrieval Quality in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Salemi, A.; Zamani, H.
abstract: SIGIR 2024 paper on RAG retrieval quality evaluation. IR-venue reference for evaluation methodology, complementary to AgentHallu-Bench's end-to-end agent evaluation.

title: The Viability of Crowdsourcing for RAG Evaluation
authors: (authors, 2025)
abstract: SIGIR 2025 paper on crowdsourcing RAG evaluation with human and LLM judgments. Directly adjacent to AgentHallu-Bench's human-vs-ensemble-vs-heuristic judge comparison.

title: Large Language Models as Assessors: On the Impact of Relevance Scales
authors: (authors, 2025)
abstract: Studies how relevance scale choice affects LLMs-as-assessors. Direct IR evaluation reference on judge reliability with practical implications.

title: LLM-assisted Relevance Assessments: When Should We Ask LLMs for Help?
authors: Takehi, R.; Voorhees, E. M.; Sakai, T.; Soboroff, I.
abstract: SIGIR 2025 paper on when to use LLMs for relevance assessments. Includes Ellen Voorhees and Ian Soboroff — authoritative IR-community voices. Key reference for the IP&M audience.

title: A Human-AI Comparative Analysis of Prompt Sensitivity in LLM-based Relevance Judgment
authors: Arabzadeh, N.; Clarke, C. L. A.
abstract: Compares human and AI prompt sensitivity in relevance judgments. Supports AgentHallu-Bench's documented conservative bias of ensemble judges — LLM judges differ systematically from humans.

title: Synthetic Test Collections for Retrieval Evaluation
authors: Rahmani, H. A.; Craswell, N.; Yilmaz, E.; Mitra, B.; Campos, D.
abstract: Synthetic test collections for retrieval evaluation using LLMs. Relevant for AgentHallu-Bench's synthetic trace release and evaluation methodology.

title: Survey and Analysis of Hallucinations in Large Language Models: Attribution to Prompting Strategies or Model Behavior
authors: Anh-Hoang; Tran; Nguyen
abstract: Attribution framework for hallucination — does it stem from prompting or model behavior? Published in peer-reviewed journal. Supporting reference for attribution-focused framing.

title: Hallucination Detection and Mitigation in Large Language Models
authors: Dahl, C.; and co-authors
abstract: Recent survey of hallucination detection and mitigation in LLMs. Describes calibration, self-evaluation, and ensemble voting — relevant for AgentHallu-Bench context.

title: Large Language Models Hallucination: A Comprehensive Survey
authors: Alansari, A.; Luqman, H.
abstract: Comprehensive taxonomy and analysis of hallucination causes, detection, and mitigation across the LLM development lifecycle. Complementary survey to Huang et al. 2024 TOIS.

title: Large Language Models Present New Questions for Decision Support
authors: (authors, 2024)
abstract: Top IS journal treating LLMs as decision support. Useful IS-venue citation for the practical-implications section.

title: Large Language Model in Creative Work: The Role of Collaboration Modality and User Expertise
authors: Chen, Z.; Chan, J.
abstract: Management Science paper on LLM collaboration modality and user expertise. IS-adjacent high-impact journal reference for practical implications.

title: The LiveRAG Challenge at SIGIR 2025
authors: Carmel, D.; and co-authors
abstract: SIGIR 2025 RAG challenge — live evaluation of RAG systems with standardized generation model (Falcon3-10B). Precedent for controlled RAG evaluation environments.

title: Are You Hallucinated? Insights into Large Language Models
authors: (authors)
abstract: ScienceDirect journal paper on LLM hallucination via extrapolative reasoning experiments with Gemini models. Elsevier-family journal, useful for IP&M context.

title: Hallucinations of Large Multimodal Models: Problem and Countermeasures
authors: (authors)
abstract: Elsevier Information Fusion journal paper — sibling journal to IP&M — on hallucinations in large multimodal models with RL-based countermeasures. Venue-appropriate for IP&M citations.

title: Internal Representations as Indicators of Hallucinations in Agent Tool Selection
authors: (authors)
abstract: Uses internal model representations to indicate hallucinations specifically in agent tool selection. Close methodological sibling to AgentHallu-Bench's parameter-stage analysis.

title: Landis-Koch Benchmark for Kappa Interpretation
authors: Landis, J. R.; Koch, G. G.
abstract: Foundational benchmark for Cohen's κ interpretation: slight (<0.2), fair (0.2–0.4), moderate (0.4–0.6), substantial (0.6–0.8), almost perfect (>0.8). Required citation whenever AgentHallu-Bench reports κ.

title: Coefficient of Agreement for Nominal Scales
authors: Cohen, J.
abstract: Original Cohen's κ paper. Required foundational citation for any κ reporting in AgentHallu-Bench.

title: Agentic AI and Large Language Models in Radiology: Opportunities and Hallucination Challenges
authors: (authors)
abstract: Survey of agentic AI in radiology addressing hallucination risk and multi-agent mitigation. Use for medical-domain framing of AgentHallu-Bench's medical task subset.

title: Towards Reliable Trajectories in Agentic IR: Beyond Fluency
authors: Sinha, A.; and co-authors
abstract: Argues for trajectory-level perspective with verification gates, causal attribution, and calibrated abstention in agentic IR. Directly aligned with AgentHallu-Bench's stage-decomposition philosophy.

title: Sherlock: Reliable and Efficient Agentic Workflow Execution with Selective Verification
authors: (authors)
abstract: Selective verification and speculative execution for agentic workflow reliability. Comparison point for AgentHallu-Bench's interceptor but more complex architecture.

title: Diagnosing LLM Hallucinations in Process Mining Tasks
authors: (authors)
abstract: Domain-specific hallucination benchmark for process mining using LLM-as-judge with taxonomy-based audit. Methodologically adjacent to AgentHallu-Bench's evaluation-critique story.
